title: Only 6% Of Adults Can Pass This Air Force Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Flight Foundations, Controls and Headings, Aviation Language, Airflow and Navigation, Flight Physics across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Know what keeps aircraft flying?
Put your knowledge to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Flight Foundations, Controls and Headings, Aviation Language, Airflow and Navigation, Flight Physics. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an official military recruitment, aptitude, medical or eligibility assessment for any country.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

airforce-q1.question: In straight-and-level flight, which force acts upward against weight?

airforce-q2.question: Which cockpit instrument indicates an aircraft’s altitude?

airforce-round1-new1.question: Which force opposes an aircraft's motion through the air?

airforce-round1-new2.question: What does thrust primarily help an aircraft do?

airforce-round1-new3.question: Which instrument shows pitch and bank relative to the horizon?

airforce-round1-new4.question: What does indicated airspeed primarily relate to?

answers.a3: Speed of the wind over the ground alone

airforce-q3.question: Which primary control surfaces roll a conventional airplane about its longitudinal axis?

airforce-q4.question: A magnetic heading of 270 degrees points approximately in which direction?

airforce-round2-new2.question: On a conventional airplane, which control surface primarily controls pitch?

airforce-round2-new3.question: Which direction is opposite a heading of north?

airforce-round2-new4.question: A quarter-turn clockwise from east points in which direction?

airforce-q5.question: Mach number compares an aircraft’s speed with what?

airforce-q6.question: When facing forward in an aircraft, which side is called port?

airforce-round3-new1.question: What does 'starboard' mean when facing forward?

answers.a1: Below the local speed of sound
answers.a2: Above the local speed of sound
answers.a3: Exactly twice the speed of sound

airforce-round3-new4.question: What can a headwind do to groundspeed if true airspeed is unchanged?

answers.a3: Leave it unchanged in every case

airforce-q7.question: A runway numbered 09 is aligned approximately toward which compass direction?

airforce-q8.question: What is the angle between an airfoil’s chord line and the oncoming airflow called?

airforce-round4-new1.question: An aerodynamic stall occurs when an airfoil exceeds what?

answers.a4: The speed of sound in every case

airforce-round4-new2.question: What is the chord line of an airfoil?

answers.a1: A straight line from leading edge to trailing edge
answers.a2: The aircraft's flight path on a map

airforce-round4-new3.question: Runway numbers normally relate to which quantity?

answers.a1: Magnetic direction rounded to tens of degrees
answers.a3: Number of aircraft allowed per hour

airforce-round4-new4.question: Why can magnetic and true north differ?

answers.a1: Earth's magnetic field is not aligned exactly with geographic north
answers.a3: The aircraft always points into wind
answers.a4: Latitude and longitude are the same

airforce-q9.question: Jet thrust is explained most directly by which of Newton’s laws?

airforce-q10.question: If air density stays constant and airspeed doubles, dynamic pressure changes by approximately what factor?

airforce-round5-new1.question: What does increasing air density do to dynamic pressure at a fixed airspeed?

airforce-round5-new2.question: A vehicle covers 120 km in two hours at a constant groundspeed. What is that speed?

airforce-round5-new3.question: In steady straight-and-level flight at constant speed, how do total lift and weight compare?

answers.a2: Lift must always be twice weight

airforce-round5-new4.question: Why is aircraft balance important as well as total weight?

answers.a1: The centre of gravity affects stability and control
answers.a4: Only the total weight can affect flight
